answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust accumulation: an agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero weight no matter how many clones join. Like a saffron harvest, reputation is expensive in time, not money. Each honest epoch acts as a ferrous anchor, hardening the record, while every slashing event resets progress. Attacking therefore requires a long voyage of patient, costly participation per identity, so mass fake accounts yield negligible voting or market power and are unprofitable to run at scale.
